title: pytest-xharness-eval decision record
description: One ADR, authored as data (ADR 0048). This is the librarian's shipped okf-yaml record schema adopted strictly: every field it requires is required here, and the only edits are the tightenings the convention asks an adopting repository to make -- the `ADR-` id prefix, and `group`/`tags` drawn from this repository's closed domain enum so a typo fails the build rather than creating a group of one. Nothing is relaxed. `additionalProperties` is false at every level. ADR 0047's `body` and `status_note` are gone: the argument is redistributed across `problem`, `decision` and `consequences`, and the status sentence's cross-link phrasing survives in each edge's `note`.

id.description: Record identifier. Immutable: every citation in the codebase and in prose resolves through the four digits, so renumbering is forbidden.

slug.description: The filename stem after the number. Immutable for the same reason as `id`.

plan_id.description: Optional external identifier: a planning-era id, a ticket, an upstream record. Null throughout this repository -- no record was ever raised against a planning axis -- but declared rather than absent, so the field means 'none applies' instead of 'nobody considered it'.

group.description: The record's primary domain, and the compound parent it sits in on the graph. A closed set: a new domain is a deliberate addition here, so a typo fails the build instead of silently creating a group of one. Each record has exactly one, because a compound node has exactly one parent.

title.description: The decision as a short assertion.

description.description: One-line routing summary for the index and the OKF frontmatter. Must not end in a full stop: it is a label, not a sentence. Anchored to the end rather than banning '.', or any value containing a path such as `~/.claude` would fail.

status.description: The lifecycle word. Scope -- which part of a record a later one replaced -- is carried on the edge that replaced it, in its `note`.

tags.description: The domains this record touches, primary first, drawn from the same closed set as `group`. Capped at two: a record needing three has usually not been read closely enough to say what it is mainly about.

lens.description: The reusable rule. Read this to apply the decision without opening the record.

provenance.description: The evidence the decision rests on: what forced it, in prose.

enforced_in.description: The surfaces where the decision is actually binding -- a module, a config key, a CI gate, a doc. Repository-relative paths, so a reader can open one.

relates_to.description: Typed edges over the closed vocabulary. Every relation is paired with its inverse so a validator can check symmetry; a missing inverse is reported, never failed.

note.description: What the relation means, in a clause. Carries the governing phrase from the record's original status sentence, so the scope of a supersession survives the typing.

symptom.description: What was observed. The behaviour, not the theory.

pain_point.description: What it cost, and why that cost matters.

given.description: The fact the decision rests on.

we_prefer.description: Must name the rejected alternative; the shape is 'X, over Y'.

unless.description: The escape hatch, or 'never' when the decision is unconditional.

in_practice.description: How the decision shows up in the work. Markdown block scalars: a clause that argued with a table or a fenced example keeps it here.

cons.description: A record with no cons has not been thought about.
